title: Hadith on Importance of Kinship
summary: This hadith highlights the importance of maintaining kinship ties for entering paradise and avoiding hell.
translation: The blessed Hadiths have greatly emphasized maintaining ties of kinship — fulfilling the rights of blood relatives is an important duty in Islam and a significant responsibility in humanity. If everyone attends to their relatives, no one would need to go outside their family. This hadith states that maintaining kinship is among the deeds that lead to paradise and save one from hell. Hazrat Ayub Khalib bin Ziyad Ansari (RA) narrates that a man asked, "O Messenger of Allah, tell me a deed that will admit me to paradise and keep me away from hell." The Prophet (PBUH) said: Worship Allah — don't worship anyone else. This was the first instruction. Secondly, don’t associate partners with Him. Thirdly, establish prayer — particularly adhere to obligatory ones. Fourthly, pay Zakat — it is obligatory on the wealthy and not paying it keeps this responsibility unfulfilled. Fifthly, maintain kinship. Faqih Abu Allah says that if a person persistently does these five things, immense rewards, like tall mountains, are bestowed by Allah, and sustenance increases. These acts are: continuously giving charity, even if a little; maintaining kinship; striving in the path of Allah; staying in a state of ablution; and continually obeying parents. These deeds are rewarded extensively, and the five things mentioned in the hadith are crucial. A man generally asked the Prophet (PBUH) for a deed leading to paradise and safety from hell, and maintaining kinship was one of them. It is an essential duty to treat all relatives fairly and attend to their rights and responsibilities.
